Meet Dan Laughlin
Sen. Dan Laughlin was elected to the Pennsylvania State Senate in 2016 to represent the 49th Senatorial District, which includes nearly all of Erie County. He was reelected in 2020 and 2024. Born in Erie and raised in the Erie Heights housing project, Sen. Laughlin is the son of a decorated World War II veteran. As a small business owner, Sen. Laughlin strongly supports policies that create jobs, limit government spending and ease the tax and regulatory burden on job-creators. An advocate for government reform, he is committed to making state government accessible and accountable to the people he serves.

October 2018
–
Senate Bill 1205
, a measure introduced by Laughlin that updates and streamlines reporting requirements for insurance companies in Pennsylvania received final legislative approval and is signed into law as Act 163 of 2018.

– State Budget announced with no tax increase. Funding increased for school safety and Pre-K and K through 12 public education.
June 2018
– Coordinated state agency collaboration to allow unique business to open and operate on the Bay.
June 2018
– In light of economic development efforts and City of Erie expansion projects, continued his advocacy in Harrisburg for a CRIZ designation for Erie.
May 2018
– Fought for expansion of Pre-K education funding.
May 2018
– Senate approved
Senate Bill 1031
; a measure introduced by Laughlin intended to increase government transparency by requiring the Department of Insurance to detail its spending for outside contractors. The bill stalled in the House.
April 2018
– Laughlin was awarded a Certificate of Appreciation by the SkillsUSA 1 Pennsylvania Union Foundation. SkillsUSA is a partnership of students, teachers and industry working together to ensure America has a skilled workforce.
March 2018
– Began discussions with Army Corp of Engineers to seek alternatives to break walls on Presque Isle. Goal was to find new technology to protect sand while eliminating rock piles to beautify the view.
February 2018

– After numerous meetings with volunteer firefighters throughout the 49th district, Laughlin floated ideas to train low risk prison inmates as firefighters to ease staffing issues and offer rehabilitation and redemption to individuals facing reentry.  Initiates discussion with Secretary of Corrections with the goal of creating a pilot project.

November 2017
– Laughlin joined local elected officials to fight for higher quality “Lake Street” bridge in Girard Township.  Railroad intended a redesign to a lower quality, lower cost bridge deemed unacceptable to Girard Borough and its citizens.

– The Senate approves
Senate Bill 663
, a measure introduced by Laughlin that amends the UCC act to require municipalities to contract with at least three third-party agencies to handle building inspections. The bill stalls in the House.
October 2017
– Passage of
House Bill 674
, an omnibus Fiscal Code bill, locks in the increased funding, secured by Senator Laughlin, for the Erie School District on a recurring, annual basis.
September 2017
– Amid talk of crumbling neighborhoods and financial issues, Senator hosts state senate discussion on blight and community revitalization issues. Roundtable discussion with members of the Senate Majority Policy Committee kicks off neighborhood revitalization.
July 2017
– At Laughlin’s request, the Erie School District is allocated $14 million in Educational Access Program Funding as a one-time, one-year expenditure in the Fiscal Year 2017-18 state budget.
March 2017
– The Senate approves
Senate Bill 169
, a measure introduced by Senator Laughlin, that would require lobbyists to register and file reports electronically through a computerized system developed by the Pennsylvania Department of State. The bill stalls in the House.
February 2017
– Meets with school superintendents throughout the district and starts visits to all school systems in the city and county.
January 2017
– Begins efforts to meet with and make site visits where appropriate to local businesses to gain first-hand knowledge of the challenges of operating a business in Pennsylvania.
January 2017
– As one of his first official acts in office, Laughlin calls on Governor Tom Wolf to reverse his moratorium on the expansion of Keystone Opportunity Zones and City Revitalization and Improvement Zones.
2016
December 2016
– Senator-elect Laughlin announces that — through renegotiations of the terms of the lease — he was able to create a 31% reduction in the monthly rent for the district office vacated by former Senator Sean Wiley, which represents a savings to taxpayers of $15,500 a year for the same location.

The Capitol
A National Historic Landmark
Pennsylvania's Capitol is, first and foremost, a public building belonging to the citizens of the Commonwealth. It is also a priceless architectural and artistic treasure, a majestic symbol of history and power, and an icon of democracy and freedom.
When President Theodore Roosevelt attended the dedication of the building on October 4, 1906, he said, "This is the handsomest building I ever saw." The Capitol was designed in the American Renaissance style by Philadelphia architect Joseph Huston (1866-1940), who envisioned the building as a "Palace of Art."
Built and furnished at a cost of $13 million, the Capitol features paintings, stained glass and furnishings by some of the best artisans of the day. The building incorporates various Renaissance designs in some of its largest rooms: Italian in the House Chamber, French in the Senate Chamber, and English in the Governor's Reception Room.  It also reflects Greek, Roman and Victorian influences in its art and ornamentation. Throughout the building, Huston blended the various styles with motifs featuring Pennsylvania's achievements in labor, industry and history, making the Capitol uniquely American.  Its five-story exterior is faced with handsome Vermont granite, and the roof is composed of green glazed terra cotta tile.
The Capitol's centerpiece is a spectacular 272-foot, 52 million-pound dome inspired by Michelangelo's design for St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. Following its completion, the building was the tallest structure between Philadelphia and Pittsburgh for 80 years. While the building has been modernized over time, efforts to blend form and function continue today, and a special
Capitol Preservation Committee

ensures that as the building evolves, the artistic elements are never lost. The seat of Pennsylvania's government continues to inspire visitors with its wealth of art, its outstanding architecture, and its strong connection to the vision of the Commonwealth's founder, William Penn, who sought to establish a land that would be governed by just laws and tolerant of all religious faiths.

Aimee’s Law Passes the Pennsylvania Senate
Aimee’s Law has passed the Pennsylvania Senate! My bill,
Senate Bill 1311
, would create a statewide public animal abuse registry to help keep animals out of the hands of convicted abusers.
So many of you have contacted my office asking about this bill and urging us to act. Thank you for speaking up, and thank you to my Senate colleagues for supporting this important measure.
The bill now heads to the House of Representatives. Let’s get Aimee’s Law across the finish line!
Protecting Private Property Rights
The Pennsylvania Senate has passed my bill,
Senate Bill 1431
, to strengthen protections for landowners when Pennsylvania Game Commission officers enter private property.
Our game wardens do important work, and their authority should come with clear limits that respect private property rights. This bill helps ensure those rights are protected while supporting the enforcement of our hunting and wildlife laws.
The bill now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.
Senate Passes Bill to Support Local Clubs
The Pennsylvania Senate has passed my bill,
Senate Bill 465
, to give local clubs greater flexibility in how they use proceeds from small games of chance.
These clubs bring people together, support local causes and serve our communities. My bill would help them cover operating expenses so they can keep their doors open and continue that important work.
The bill now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.
How I Can Help
If you or someone you know is having trouble accessing state programs or services, or if you have questions about a law or government program and aren’t sure where to turn, my team and I are here to help. We can guide you through the process, connect you with the right resources, and provide support on a wide range of issues to make things easier for you.
School Bus Driver Safety Bill Approved by Senate
Approximately 1.5 million children are transported on school buses every day in Pennsylvania, and the Senate approved legislation aimed at keeping reckless bus drivers from getting behind the wheel.
Senate Bill 1262
would increase penalties for school bus drivers who transport children while under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance or a dangerous combination of both.
Read more about this school bus safety measure
.
The latest Senate action follows passage last year of
Senate Bill 65
, which would increase the required stopping distance for drivers approaching from the opposite direction when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing. Both bills await passage in the House of Representatives.
Standing with Breast Cancer Survivors
I was proud to join the Pennsylvania Breast Cancer Coalition at the State Capitol as we kicked off Breast Cancer Awareness Month by turning the East Wing Fountain pink. It was especially meaningful to stand alongside breast cancer survivors and thrivers, advocates and families from across Pennsylvania who continue to bring hope and strength to this important cause.
The event was a powerful reminder of the importance of early detection and ensuring women have access to the screenings, care and support they need. And here in Pennsylvania during October, we’re reminded that breast cancer is not a red or blue issue – it’s pink. It affects every one of us. Together, we can raise awareness, support those facing breast cancer and celebrate the survivors and thrivers who inspire us every day.

Accelerating Access to Veterans’ Benefits and Employment Opportunities
Under a recent
executive order
, federal agencies must update their technology systems and policies to give veterans quicker access to the benefits they earned through their military service.
The

My bill, Senate Bill 1311, advanced from the Senate Judiciary Committee this week, bringing Aimee’s Law one step closer to passage.
Named for a six-month-old husky who died after being abandoned in the cold in Erie, the bill would establish a statewide animal abuse registry to help protect animals from convicted abusers.
I’m grateful to my colleagues for their support and will continue working to move this bill forward.
Four Bills Advance in Harrisburg
It was a busy and productive week in Harrisburg as four of my bills cleared committee:
Aimee’s Law (SB 1311)
:
Creating a public animal abuse registry to help protect animals from convicted abusers.
Supporting Local Clubs (SB 465)
:
Giving clubs greater flexibility to use small games of chance proceeds for their operations.
Protecting Private Property Rights (SB 1431)
:
Strengthening protections against warrantless searches by Game Commission officers.
Protecting Our Fisheries (SB 1213)
:
Strengthening enforcement against illegal snagging and foul hooking.
Thank you to my colleagues for supporting these measures. I’ll continue working to move them forward for Erie County and communities across Pennsylvania.

I joined city officials to highlight more than $1.17 million in Local Share Account (LSA) funding for Erie. These investments will support roof replacements at Engine 11 and Engine 13, community policing vehicles and a new public works milling machine.
I was proud to support these projects, which give our first responders and public works crews the facilities and equipment they need to serve our community.
How I Can Help
If you or someone you know is having trouble accessing state programs or services, or if you have questions about a law or government program and aren’t sure where to turn, my team and I are here to help. We can guide you through the process, connect you with the right resources, and provide support on a wide range of issues to make things easier for you.

letter
to the commission warning the changes would infringe on our constitutional rights.
The proposed regulations would have given the state more power to enter homes and businesses without a warrant, speak to students without parents present, access private health records, unilaterally impose mask mandates and more. The DOH introduced the massive, 502-page regulatory overhaul without input from the public or the General Assembly.
Although these regulations were withdrawn, we must remain vigilant – the governor’s DOH could resubmit them at any time.

Outline a corrective action plan to put poor performing AAAs into compliance with the law and department standards and regulations.

.

The program highlighted the Sight Center’s efforts to prevent blindness, provide vision rehabilitation and social support, and help individuals maintain their independence through assistive technology and other services. Thank you to Executive Director Linda Moore and the entire Sight Center team for the difference they make throughout our region.
How I Can Help
If you or someone you know is having trouble accessing state programs or services, or if you have questions about a law or government program and aren’t sure where to turn, my team and I are here to help. We can guide you through the process, connect you with the right resources, and provide support on a wide range of issues to make things easier for you.
